findings.issue_text: Broken Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses ZodString .toString() as computed keys, resulting in static '[object Object]' strings instead of dynamic key matchers, making the schema non-functional.
In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the SafeParseReturnType wrapper object is stored as the credential key instead of the parsed data, persisting the wrong object to the database.
In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, the undefined variable `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` like other adapters, which will throw a ReferenceError at runtime.

In refreshOAuthTokens.ts, returning a raw fetch Response object when credential sharing is enabled causes a return-type mismatch, breaking downstream property accesses in Hubspot, Google, and Zoho adapters.

Dead/unreachable error-handling code in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on validation failure, making the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch unreachable.
No HTTP method restriction in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, accepts any method and unconditionally parses `req.body`
`parse` used instead of `safeParse` for schema validation in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, causing unhandled 500 errors on invalid input
Missing error handling for `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, causing crashes if decryption or parsing fails
Webhook secret compared using `!==` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, creating a timing-attack vulnerability
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is broken in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` because `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to `"[object Object]"` instead of a dynamic key
Missing `refresh_token` is replaced with the literal string `"refresh_token"` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, which will be persisted and cause future failures
`refreshOAuthTokens` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns a raw `fetch` Response object, breaking callers expecting parsed typed objects or Axios responses
Salesforce's `CalendarService.ts` does not use `refreshOAuthTokens` like other services, making the credential sync feature inconsistent/incomplete
`response.statusText !== "OK"` used for error checking in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, which is unreliable; should use `response.ok` or `response.status`
`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` in `packages/lib/constants.ts` doesn't check for `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, allowing the flag to be true while the sync endpoint is unset
Hardcoded `redirectUri` to `"zoho-bigin"` in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` instead of using `appConfig.slug`, breaking OAuth redirect if slug differs
No handling for team credentials in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, as it only looks up credentials by `userId` instead of also considering `teamId`
Unrelated change in zoho-bigin redirect URI from `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded "zoho-bigin" string bundled into this PR
Salesforce does not use `refreshOAuthTokens` for token refresh, preventing credentials from syncing when credential sharing is enabled
Several apps (Hubspot, Lark, Webex, Zoho-Bigin, ZohoCRM) use `refreshOAuthTokens` but not `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, causing validation failures when sync is enabled
`refreshOAuthTokens` returns incompatible types depending on code path (AxiosResponse vs fetch Response), breaking Zoho-Bigin and ZohoCRM when sync is enabled
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` in `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`) incorrectly, failing to match arbitrary numeric properties as intended
Webhook handler does not restrict HTTP method to POST, allowing other methods like GET to reach credential validation and database-write logic
`refreshOAuthTokens` returns inconsistent types between branches, returning a raw `Response` or what `refreshFunction()` returns, breaking consumers expecting specific types
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys that evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, resulting in a schema that does not validate real OAuth fields
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `SafeParseResult` but Google Calendar stores it directly as the credential key, persisting a wrapper object instead of actual credentials
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` substitutes the literal string `"refresh_token"` for missing refresh tokens, guaranteeing future hard-to-diagnose failures
Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method instead of restricting to POST
Webhook secret comparison uses `!==` instead of constant-time comparison, making it vulnerable to timing attacks
No try/catch around `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` in the webhook, risking unhandled exceptions and generic 500s with sensitive stack traces
`refreshOAuthTokens` reads `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` directly instead of using the centralized `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` constant, splitting env-var ownership
Salesforce `CalendarService` unconditionally refreshes the access token on every instantiation, wasting API quota and adding latency
`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used to index `req.headers` without validation or normalization, causing 403s for self-hosters who configure non-lowercase header names
`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` lacks validation that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is 32 bytes, causing runtime decryption failures instead of failing fast at startup

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as computed object keys, producing '[object Object]' instead of dynamic keys, resulting in a malformed schema that won't match real token responses

When refresh_token is missing from the response, the code assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the token value instead of preserving the existing refresh token or handling the absence differently

When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw Response from fetch() but callers expect different return types (e.g., res?.data, HubspotToken object, Axios response), causing type mismatches and runtime failures
Zoho Bigin's CalendarService.ts passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens while every other caller passes credential.userId, which is inconsistent and likely a bug

Salesforce CalendarService.ts performs a full token refresh unconditionally on every connection construction without checking if the existing access token is still valid, adding unnecessary latency and API calls

app-credential.ts imports z as a default import (import z from 'zod') while all other files use named imports (import { z } from 'zod'), which will fail if the project's zod version doesn't provide a default export

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the result of .safeParse() but when credential sharing is enabled and the minimum schema is used, refreshTokenResponse.data has type unknown, yet line 24 mutates .data.refresh_token directly, which TypeScript would flag and the schema doesn't define refresh_token as a field

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No HTTP method restriction in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, accepts any method and unconditionally parses `req.body`

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` API route, the `handler` does not check `req.method` (e.g., `POST`) before proceeding. After the header/feature-flag checks, it unconditionally executes `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For non-body methods like `GET`, `req.body` will typically be `undefined`, causing `zod` to throw and the route to return a 500 instead of a proper 405/400. This is a concrete correctness/robustness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing error handling for `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, causing crashes if decryption or parsing fails

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` without any try/catch or validation. Both `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` can throw on malformed ciphertext, wrong/missing env key (empty string fallback), or non-JSON plaintext. Since the function doesn’t handle these exceptions, the API route will error out (500) rather than returning a controlled response, making it trivially triggerable by a bad request body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared using `!==` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, creating a timing-attack vulnerability
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is broken in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` because `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to `"[object Object]"` instead of a dynamic key

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema` the computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are evaluated immediately to a single string key (very likely `"[object Object]"` or similar), not a dynamic/index signature. `z.object({...})` does not support “any string key with number value” this way; it would need `z.record(...)` or `.catchall(...)`. As written, the schema only defines a literal property with that computed name, so it will not actually validate/allow arbitrary numeric expiry fields (e.g. `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing `refresh_token` is replaced with the literal string `"refresh_token"` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, which will be persisted and cause future failures
`refreshOAuthTokens` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns a raw `fetch` Response object, breaking callers expecting parsed typed objects or Axios responses

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `refreshOAuthTokens`, when syncing is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is the raw `fetch(...)` `Response`. Several callers in the diff expect non-`Response` shapes:
- `GoogleCalendarService`: `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` This matches the previous google-auth-library `refreshToken()` result (`{ res }` with `res.data`), but a `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so token extraction will be `undefined` and break refresh.
- `HubspotCalendarService`: assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`; if syncing is enabled this will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken` object.
So the wrapper returning a raw `Response` does break callers expecting parsed/typed token objects or Axios-style responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No handling for team credentials in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, as it only looks up credentials by `userId` instead of also considering `teamId`

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler explicitly defines a request body schema containing only `userId`, `appSlug`, and `keys`, and the comments state it is the “UserId of the cal.com user”. The DB lookup/update is intentionally scoped to `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and it also verifies the `user` exists via `prisma.user.findUnique`. Nothing in the diff indicates this endpoint is intended to support team-owned credentials, nor is there any `teamId` in the payload or any team-related logic introduced elsewhere in this handler. Therefore, claiming “no handling for team credentials” is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff; it’s a feature request/assumption about requirements not shown here.

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns incompatible types depending on code path (AxiosResponse vs fetch Response), breaking Zoho-Bigin and ZohoCRM when sync is enabled
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` in `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`) incorrectly, failing to match arbitrary numeric properties as intended

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. These computed keys do not create a “match any key” rule in Zod/TypeScript; they evaluate to a single literal property name (whatever `z.string().toString()` returns at runtime, e.g. "[object Object]"), so the schema will not accept arbitrary numeric properties like `expires_in`/`expiry_date` as intended. The correct approach would use Zod features like `.catchall(...)`, `.passthrough()`, or `z.record(...)` rather than computed object keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler does not restrict HTTP method to POST, allowing other methods like GET to reach credential validation and database-write logic

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler runs for any HTTP method and there is no `req.method` check (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). As written, non-POST requests (GET/PUT/etc.) can reach the webhook secret check and then attempt `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, and if the header/secret matches and a body is provided/parsed, they can proceed to the credential create/update database-write logic. The absence of an HTTP method restriction is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns inconsistent types between branches, returning a raw `Response` or what `refreshFunction()` returns, breaking consumers expecting specific types

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` has two branches with different return shapes: when syncing is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is a `fetch(...)` Response, but otherwise it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns. Several call sites assume a non-`Response` type (e.g. Google Calendar treats the result as an object with `.data` (`const token = res?.data;`), and Hubspot assigns the result to `HubspotToken`). If the sync branch runs, those consumers will receive a raw `Response` (no `.data`, not a `HubspotToken`), causing runtime/type breakage. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys that evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, resulting in a schema that does not validate real OAuth fields

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is declared as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS object literal, computed keys must evaluate to a concrete string/symbol at definition time; `z.string().toString()` does not create a dynamic “any key”/index signature, it produces a single fixed property name (commonly something like "[object Object]" or another constant). This means the schema will (a) not validate arbitrary OAuth fields as intended and (b) may even overwrite one computed key with the other since they likely stringify to the same value. Proper Zod patterns would be `z.object({access_token: ...}).catchall(...)` or `z.record(...)`. So the finding describes a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `SafeParseResult` but Google Calendar stores it directly as the credential key, persisting a wrapper object instead of actual credentials
matched_golden_ids: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParseResult wrapper and that the code stores/persists this wrapper directly as the credential key instead of the parsed credentials payload, which is the same core issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method instead of restricting to POST

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` does not check `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). Next.js API routes will invoke this handler for any HTTP method by default, so the endpoint effectively accepts GET/PUT/etc. With non-POST methods, `req.body` may be missing/invalid and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` will throw (uncaught), but there is still no explicit method restriction as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret comparison uses `!==` instead of constant-time comparison, making it vulnerable to timing attacks

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authentication checks `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is a normal JavaScript string inequality comparison, not a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`). For shared-secret verification, non-constant-time comparison can leak information via timing side-channels, so the diff does introduce exactly what the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No try/catch around `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` in the webhook, risking unhandled exceptions and generic 500s with sensitive stack traces

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the code directly does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` without any try/catch or validation. Both `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (e.g., wrong/empty `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, malformed ciphertext) and `JSON.parse(...)` (non-JSON plaintext) can throw. Since the handler doesn’t catch these errors, the route can crash into an unhandled exception and return a generic 500 instead of a controlled 4xx error. The “sensitive stack traces” part depends on environment/logging, but the unhandled-exception/500 risk is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` reads `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` directly instead of using the centralized `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` constant, splitting env-var ownership

adjudication.rationale:
The diff shows `refreshOAuthTokens` checks **both** `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`:

```ts
if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId) {
  ...
}
```

So it is not using the env var *instead of* the centralized constant; it already uses the constant as part of the gating logic. Also, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (a feature flag) is not a substitute for the endpoint value; the endpoint must come from an env var anyway. The proposed finding misreads the code and doesn’t identify a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used to index `req.headers` without validation or normalization, causing 403s for self-hosters who configure non-lowercase header names

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes `req.headers` with `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` directly:

```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]
```

In Node/Next.js, incoming header names are normalized to lowercase in `req.headers`. If a self-hoster configures `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` with any uppercase characters (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), this lookup will not match the lowercase key (e.g. `calcom-webhook-secret`), resulting in `undefined !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and an incorrect 403. The diff adds only a comment suggesting lowercase but no validation/normalization, so the reported issue is a real, verifiable correctness problem introduced by this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` lacks validation that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is 32 bytes, causing runtime decryption failures instead of failing fast at startup

adjudication.rationale: In the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` handler, decrypted keys are obtained via `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and then `JSON.parse(...)`. There is no validation that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set or that it matches the documented 32-byte requirement for AES-256 (the code even falls back to an empty string). If `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true and the env var is missing/incorrect length, decryption will fail at request time (likely throwing and producing a runtime error) rather than failing fast with a clear startup/config error. This lack of validation is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as computed object keys, producing '[object Object]' instead of dynamic keys, resulting in a malformed schema that won't match real token responses

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object, and calling `.toString()` on it yields a literal string (typically `"[object Object]"`), not a dynamic/pattern key. This produces a schema with an actual property named `"[object Object]"` (and the second one likely collides/overrides), not “any string key with number value”. As a result the schema does not do what the comments intend and will not correctly validate real OAuth token responses; Zod requires `.catchall(...)`, `.passthrough()`, or a `z.record(...)` pattern for that behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When refresh_token is missing from the response, the code assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the token value instead of preserving the existing refresh token or handling the absence differently

When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw Response from fetch() but callers expect different return types (e.g., res?.data, HubspotToken object, Axios response), causing type mismatches and runtime failures

adjudication.rationale:
The new `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch()` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, but otherwise returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often a non-Response object). Call sites now assume the old shapes:
- In `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code does `const token = res?.data;` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. A `fetch()` `Response` has no `.data` property, so in sync mode this will make `token` undefined and likely crash when accessing `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`.
- In `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is assigned to `HubspotToken`. In sync mode it would instead be a `Response`, so downstream usage as a token object will fail at runtime.
Other callers (Office365/Lark) expect a `Response` and would be compatible, highlighting the inconsistent return type problem introduced by the wrapper.
